title: Special Act on the Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste
full_text:
Special Act on the Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to enhance democracy, accountability, and transparency in the management of high-level radioactive waste and to contribute to the safety of the people and future generations by prescribing principles and procedures for the safe management of high-level radioactive waste and matters necessary for the selection of sites for high-level radioactive waste management facilities, etc.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows:
1. The term "high-level radioactive waste" means radioactive waste under subparagraph 18 of Article 2 of the Nuclear Safety Act whose radioactivity concentration and heat generation rate are at or above the values determined by the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission established under Article 3 of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission.
2. The term "spent nuclear fuel" means nuclear fuel material used as fuel in a nuclear reactor or nuclear fuel material subjected to nuclear fission by other means: Provided, That spent nuclear fuel determined to be disposed of under Article 36-2 of the Nuclear Safety Act shall be deemed high-level radioactive waste under subparagraph 1.
3. The term "management of high-level radioactive waste" means activities involving the acceptance of high-level radioactive waste for storage or disposal and all activities incidental thereto, including transportation and safety analysis and evaluation.
4. The term "storage" means keeping high-level radioactive waste or spent nuclear fuel for a certain period until its disposal.
5. The term "disposal" means permanently isolating high-level radioactive waste from the human living environment.
6. The term "high-level radioactive waste management facilities" means the following facilities and their ancillary facilities for the management of high-level radioactive waste:
(a) Interim storage facilities for high-level radioactive waste: Facilities for storing high-level radioactive waste received and transported from persons generating such waste until its disposal, excluding spent nuclear fuel storage facilities on nuclear power plant sites;
(b) High-level radioactive waste disposal facilities: Facilities for disposing of high-level radioactive waste received and transported from persons generating such waste or from interim storage facilities for high-level radioactive waste;
(c) Underground research facilities within the site of a high-level radioactive waste disposal facility: Facilities for researching and demonstrating the performance of factors related to the safety of disposal facilities, including the geological characteristics of the site, in the underground environment of the site on which a high-level radioactive waste disposal facility is to be constructed.
7. The term "spent nuclear fuel storage facilities on nuclear power plant sites" means facilities for storing spent nuclear fuel generated at a nuclear power plant within the nuclear power plant site until it is delivered to an interim storage facility for high-level radioactive waste or a high-level radioactive waste disposal facility: Provided, That facilities installed under an operating license granted pursuant to the former part of Article 20 (1) of the Nuclear Safety Act shall be excluded.
8. The term "underground research facilities for research purposes" means facilities constructed before the selection of a site for a high-level radioactive waste disposal facility to study the performance and safety of a disposal system under conditions similar to the geological environment of a disposal facility and to conduct necessary technology development, etc.

Article 3 (Relationship with Other Acts)
Except as provided in this Act, the Radioactive Waste Management Act, the Nuclear Safety Act, and the Nuclear Energy Promotion Act shall apply to the management of high-level radioactive waste.

Article 4 (Duties of the State and Local Governments)
(1) The State shall be responsible for ensuring the safety of the people by safely managing high-level radioactive waste, including endeavoring to secure high-level radioactive waste disposal facilities promptly on the basis of technologies whose safety has been verified.
(2) In formulating and implementing plans for the management of high-level radioactive waste, the State shall establish measures for safe management based on democratic procedures and scientific rationality and shall ensure that sufficient and transparent information is provided.
(3) In managing high-level radioactive waste, the State shall enable various stakeholders to express their opinions and reach a consensus through public deliberation by coordinating their interests.
(4) The State shall take necessary measures for the management of high-level radioactive waste in a manner that does not impose burdens on future generations.
(5) The State shall manage high-level radioactive waste generated in Korea in harmony with international norms and other statutes and regulations and shall establish and secure safety and security systems to enable its safe management.
(6) Local governments shall endeavor to facilitate the performance of affairs relating to the management of high-level radioactive waste, including the selection of sites for and the construction and operation of high-level radioactive waste management facilities (hereinafter referred to as "management facilities").
(7) The State and local governments shall cooperate with each other to smoothly and efficiently carry out projects for the management of high-level radioactive waste.

Article 5 (Duties of Generators of High-Level Radioactive Waste and the Management Operator)
(1) Persons generating high-level radioactive waste (hereinafter referred to as "generators of high-level radioactive waste") and the high-level radioactive waste management operator under Article 38 (hereinafter referred to as the "management operator") shall safely manage high-level radioactive waste by complying with statutes and regulations relating to nuclear safety and cooperating with institutions concerned with nuclear safety regulation.
(2) Generators of high-level radioactive waste and the management operator shall transparently disclose to the public major matters concerning the management of high-level radioactive waste and the selection of sites for and the construction and operation of management facilities.
(3) Generators of high-level radioactive waste and the management operator shall cooperate with local governments and local residents to minimize conflicts that may arise in the course of managing high-level radioactive waste and selecting sites for and constructing and operating management facilities.
(4) Generators of high-level radioactive waste shall cooperate with local governments and local residents to minimize conflicts that may arise before high-level radioactive waste is delivered to the management operator.

CHAPTER II HIGH-LEVEL RADIOACTIVE WASTE MANAGEMENT COMMISSION, ETC.

Article 6 (Establishment of the High-Level Radioactive Waste Management Commission)
(1) A High-Level Radioactive Waste Management Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Commission") shall be established under the Prime Minister to independently perform affairs necessary for the management of high-level radioactive waste and the investigation and selection of sites for management facilities, etc.
(2) The Commission shall remain in existence for five years from the date this Act enters into force: Provided, That within that period, the Government shall review whether to change the Commission into a central administrative agency under Article 2 of the Government Organization Act and report its review to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.

Article 7 (Affairs under the Jurisdiction of the Commission)
(1) The affairs under the jurisdiction of the Commission shall be as follows:
1. Matters concerning the basic direction of policies for the management of high-level radioactive waste and the formulation and implementation of related plans;
2. Matters concerning the selection of sites for management facilities and the cancellation of such selection;
3. Matters concerning the construction and operation of management facilities;
4. Matters concerning research and development and the fostering of professional personnel for the management of high-level radioactive waste;
5. Other matters prescribed as affairs of the Commission by this Act or other Acts.
(2) Details concerning the affairs under the jurisdiction of the Commission pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 8 (Composition of the Commission)
(1) The Commission shall consist of nine members, including the Chairperson, and the Chairperson and one other member shall be standing members.
(2) The Chairperson shall be a public official in political service.
(3) Members shall be appointed or commissioned from among the following persons:
1. Persons with extensive knowledge and experience in nuclear energy or the environment;
2. Persons who have engaged or are engaging in affairs relating to radiation safety or radioactive waste management.
(4) The Chairperson shall be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the Prime Minister; four members, including one standing member, shall be appointed or commissioned by the President upon the recommendation of the Chairperson; and the remaining four members shall be appointed or commissioned by the President upon the recommendation of the National Assembly.
(5) The term of office of members shall be three years, and they may serve one further consecutive term: Provided, That the term of a member newly commissioned following the resignation of a member or for a similar reason shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term.
(6) Where specialized examination is necessary to investigate and research the affairs specified in the subparagraphs of Article 7 (1), the Commission may establish specialized committees for each field.
(7) Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Commission and specialized committees for each field, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (6), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 9 (Chairperson)
(1) The Chairperson shall represent the Commission, preside over its meetings, and exercise overall control over the affairs under its jurisdiction.
(2) Where the Chairperson is unable to perform duties for an unavoidable reason, the standing member and then the other members shall act on behalf of the Chairperson in the order predetermined by the Chairperson.

Article 10 (Independence in Performing Duties and Guarantee of Status of Members)
(1) The Commission shall independently perform the affairs within its authority.
(2) No member shall be dismissed or relieved of appointment against the member's will except in any of the following cases:
1. Where the member becomes unable to perform duties due to a physical or mental disability;
2. Where the member has engaged in misconduct in connection with duties;
3. Where the member is deemed unsuitable to serve as a member due to neglect of duties, damage to dignity, or other reasons;
4. Where the member falls under any ground for disqualification under Article 11.

Article 11 (Grounds for Disqualification)
(1) None of the following persons may become a member:
1. A person falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
2. A person registered as a candidate, including a preliminary candidate, in an election held under the Public Official Election Act;
3. A member of a political party under Article 22 of the Political Parties Act.
(2) A member who comes to fall under any of the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) shall retire from office by operation of law: Provided, That the proviso to subparagraph 1 of Article 69 of the State Public Officials Act shall apply mutatis mutandis in the case of paragraph (1) 1.

Article 12 (Prohibition on Concurrent Offices of Members)
(1) While in office, a member shall not concurrently hold any of the following offices or engage in any of the following duties:
1. The office of a member of the National Assembly or a local council;
2. Other offices or duties prescribed by rules of the Commission.
(2) No member shall join a political party or engage in political activities.

Article 13 (Meetings of the Commission)
(1) A meeting of the Commission shall be held where at least two incumbent members request that a meeting be convened or where the Chairperson deems it necessary.
(2) A meeting of the Commission shall be convened with the attendance of a majority of incumbent members, and resolutions shall be passed with the affirmative vote of a majority of members present.

Article 14 (Preparation and Disclosure of Minutes)
(1) The minutes of meetings of the Commission and the specialized committees for each field shall be prepared by stenography.
(2) As a rule, the minutes under paragraph (1) shall be disclosed to the public. However, matters prescribed by Presidential Decree may be withheld from disclosure by resolution of the Commission.

Article 15 (Establishment of a Secretariat)
(1) A Secretariat shall be established within the Commission to handle its affairs and facilitate communication with the public.
(2) Matters necessary for the organization and operation of the Secretariat under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16 (Cooperation with Relevant Agencies, Etc.)
(1) Where necessary to perform the duties specified in the subparagraphs of Article 7(1), the Commission may request any of the following from the heads of relevant administrative agencies or relevant institutions:
1. Attendance before the Commission or presentation of opinions by relevant public officials or executives and employees;
2. Submission of materials or opinions necessary for the investigation and selection of sites for management facilities;
3. Submission of the results of investigations, research, or reviews concerning management facilities;
4. Submission of review opinions on agenda items referred to the Commission.
(2) The head of a relevant administrative agency or relevant institution who receives a request under any subparagraph of paragraph (1) shall comply with the request unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(3) Before applying for permission concerning the site selection, construction, operation, etc. of management facilities, the Commission shall hear the opinion of the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission under Article 3 of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission on regulatory matters for ensuring safety.

Article 17 (Master Plan for the Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste, Etc.)
(1) For the safe management of high-level radioactive waste, the Commission shall endeavor to enable interim storage facilities for high-level radioactive waste to commence operation before 2050 and disposal facilities for high-level radioactive waste to commence operation before 2060.
(2) The Commission shall establish, every five years, a master plan for the management of high-level radioactive waste covering a planning period of 30 years (hereinafter referred to as the "master plan") to manage high-level radioactive waste safely and systematically.
(3) The master plan shall include the following matters:
1. Matters concerning basic policies and measures for the management of high-level radioactive waste;
2. Matters concerning the current status and outlook of high-level radioactive waste generation and plans for its storage and disposal;
3. Matters concerning the selection of sites for management facilities and facility plans;
4. Matters concerning investment plans for management facilities;
5. Matters concerning the installation and operation of spent nuclear fuel storage facilities within the sites of nuclear power plants;
6. Matters concerning technology development, the training of personnel, etc. for the safe and efficient management of high-level radioactive waste;
7. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary for the management of high-level radioactive waste.
(4) Where the Commission intends to establish the master plan, it shall consult in advance with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies. The same shall apply where it intends to amend an established master plan.
(5) The establishment and amendment of the master plan shall be finalized following deliberation and resolution by the Nuclear Energy Promotion Commission under Article 3 of the Nuclear Energy Promotion Act. However, this shall not apply to amendments to minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(6) When establishing the master plan, the Commission shall make a draft available for public inspection in advance and collect opinions from the public. In such cases, the Commission shall hold a public hearing if so requested by the Mayor of a Special Self-Governing City, the Governor of a Special Self-Governing Province (excluding the Governor of a Special Self-Governing Province that has, within its jurisdiction, a Si or Gun that is a local government; hereinafter the same shall apply), the Mayor of a Si, the head of a Gun, or the head of a Gu (meaning the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter collectively referred to as the "head of a Si/Gun/Gu") having jurisdiction over a Special Self-Governing City, Special Self-Governing Province (excluding a Special Self-Governing Province that has, within its jurisdiction, a Si or Gun that is a local government; hereinafter the same shall apply), Si, Gun, or autonomous Gu (hereinafter referred to as a "Si/Gun/Gu") in which management facilities are under construction or in operation or which has been selected as a site for management facilities, or by residents falling within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(7) Where the Commission establishes or amends the master plan, it shall report it without delay to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.
(8) Other matters necessary for establishing the master plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Public Deliberation, Etc.)
(1) The Commission may conduct a procedure for collecting a broad range of opinions from interested parties, experts, the general public, etc. (hereinafter in this Article referred to as "public deliberation") on matters on which social conflict is anticipated in the course of establishing the master plan, managing high-level radioactive waste, etc.
(2) The Commission may establish a public deliberation committee that operates on a temporary basis (hereinafter in this Article referred to as the "Public Deliberation Committee") for public deliberation. In such cases, the functions and the period of activities of the Public Deliberation Committee shall be determined by resolution of the Commission.
(3) The Public Deliberation Committee shall consist of not more than 15 members, including one Chairperson.
(4) The Chairperson shall appoint the Chairperson and members of the Public Deliberation Committee from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience concerning the matters handled by the Public Deliberation Committee, following a recommendation and resolution by the Commission.
(5) The Chairperson of the Public Deliberation Committee may appoint advisory members from among persons with specialized knowledge and experience in relevant fields to obtain advice on agenda items submitted to the Public Deliberation Committee.
(6) Upon expiration of its period of activities, the Public Deliberation Committee may, following a resolution, submit recommendations to the Commission. In such cases, the Commission shall respect the recommendations to the greatest extent possible.
(7) The Commission may provide administrative and financial support necessary for the activities of the Public Deliberation Committee.
(8) Other matters necessary for the operation, etc. of the Public Deliberation Committee shall be determined by resolution of the Public Deliberation Committee.

Article 19 (Implementation Plan for the Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste)
(1) A management operator shall establish and implement an implementation plan for the management of high-level radioactive waste (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") each year in accordance with the master plan.
(2) When establishing an implementation plan, a management operator shall submit it to the Commission and obtain its approval; the same shall apply when amending approved matters. However, when amending minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, the management operator shall file a report with the Commission.
(3) The procedures for approval and reporting under paragraph (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER III SITE SUITABILITY SURVEYS AND SELECTION OF SITES FOR MANAGEMENT FACILITIES, ETC.

Article 20 (Establishment of Site Suitability Survey Plans)
(1) The Commission shall establish a site suitability survey plan to ensure that surveys of the suitability of sites for management facilities are conducted fairly.
(2) The establishment or amendment of a site suitability survey plan by the Commission shall be subject to deliberation and resolution by the Commission. However, this shall not apply to amendments to minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) A site suitability survey plan shall include the following matters:
1. Matters concerning the outline of site suitability surveys, including their purposes and schedules;
2. Matters concerning the procedures, methods, and evaluation criteria for site suitability surveys;
3. Matters concerning the collection of opinions from residents in areas subject to site suitability surveys;
4. Matters concerning the disclosure of information in the course of site suitability surveys;
5. Other matters that the Commission deems necessary for site suitability surveys.
(4) When establishing the evaluation criteria under paragraph (3), subparagraph 2, the Commission shall consider the standards, etc. established by the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission under Article 3 of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the Nuclear Safety and Security Commission so as to ensure the stability of management facilities and minimize their environmental impact.
(5) Where the Commission establishes or amends a site suitability survey plan, it shall report it without delay to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.

Article 21 (Preliminary Site Suitability Surveys)
(1) After surveying geological characteristics, stability, etc. throughout the national territory, the Commission shall exclude unsuitable areas and identify candidate sites for preliminary site suitability surveys (meaning surveys of surface and deep subsurface geology to ascertain the general characteristics of the siting environment) (hereinafter referred to as "candidate sites for preliminary surveys"). However, hosting areas under Article 3(1) of the Special Act on Support for Areas Hosting Low- and Intermediate-Level Radioactive Waste Disposal Facilities shall be excluded from candidate sites for preliminary surveys.
(2) The Commission shall, upon applications from the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the candidate sites for preliminary surveys identified under paragraph (1), select sites to be subject to preliminary site suitability surveys (hereinafter referred to as "sites subject to preliminary surveys").
(3) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu who intends to apply for a preliminary site suitability survey under paragraph (2) shall ascertain the opinions of local residents in advance and obtain the consent of the relevant local council. However, if the candidate site for preliminary surveys satisfies the requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree in relation to another adjacent Si/Gun/Gu, the head shall consult with the head of the adjacent Si/Gun/Gu concerned.
(4) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures, etc. for applying for preliminary site suitability surveys under paragraphs (2) and (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(5) If the head of a Si/Gun/Gu requests the provision of materials concerning site suitability, the safety of management facilities, support for the area, etc. in order to ascertain the opinions of local residents or consult with the head of an adjacent Si/Gun/Gu under paragraph (3), the Commission shall comply unless there is a justifiable reason not to do so.
(6) The Commission shall conduct preliminary site suitability surveys of the sites subject to preliminary surveys selected under paragraph (2).
(7) When a preliminary site suitability survey is completed, the Commission shall report its results without delay to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.

Article 22 (In-Depth Site Suitability Surveys)
(1) The Commission shall evaluate the results of the preliminary site suitability surveys conducted under Article 21(6) and identify sites for in-depth site suitability surveys (meaning detailed surveys of surface and deep subsurface geology, based on the results of preliminary surveys, to ascertain the detailed characteristics of the siting environment) (hereinafter referred to as "sites subject to in-depth surveys").
(2) The Commission shall conduct in-depth site suitability surveys of the sites subject to in-depth surveys identified under paragraph (1).
(3) When an in-depth site suitability survey is completed, the Commission shall report its results without delay to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.

Article 23 (Selection of Sites for Management Facilities)
(1) The Commission shall evaluate the results of the in-depth site suitability surveys conducted under Article 22(2) and identify proposed sites for management facilities.
(2) The Commission shall select sites for management facilities through its deliberation and resolution after local referendums under Article 8 of the Residents' Voting Act have been held in the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the proposed sites for management facilities identified under paragraph (1) and the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) Where proposed sites for management facilities are identified under paragraph (1), the Commission shall, without delay, notify the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over such sites and the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree of that fact and report it to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly. The same shall apply where sites for management facilities are selected under paragraph (2).

Article 24 (Establishment of the Support Committee for Areas Hosting Management Facilities)
(1) A Support Committee for Areas Hosting Management Facilities (hereinafter referred to as the "Support Committee") shall be established under the Prime Minister to deliberate on important matters concerning support for areas within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree comprising the areas hosting sites for management facilities selected under Article 23(2) and their surrounding areas, as well as areas where preliminary or in-depth site suitability surveys have been conducted (hereinafter referred to as "areas hosting management facilities, etc.").
(2) The Support Committee shall consist of not more than 20 members, including one Chairperson, and its members shall consist of ex officio members and appointed members.
(3) The Prime Minister shall serve as Chairperson of the Support Committee; the ex officio members shall be the following persons; and the appointed members shall be persons appointed by the Prime Minister from among those with extensive knowledge and experience in local support projects. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. The Minister of Finance and Economy, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, the Minister of Planning and Budget, the Chairperson of the Commission, and the heads of other central administrative agencies prescribed by Presidential Decree;
2. The Mayor of a Special Metropolitan City, Mayor of a Metropolitan City, or Governor of a Do having jurisdiction over areas hosting management facilities, etc.;
3. The head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas hosting management facilities, etc.
(4) The term of office of appointed members shall be two years, and they may be reappointed. However, the term of office of a member newly appointed due to a member's resignation or other such reason shall be the remainder of the predecessor's term.
(5) The Support Committee shall have one secretary, who shall be the Chairperson of the Commission.
(6) A working committee shall be established within the Support Committee to ensure its efficient operation.
(7) Matters necessary for the composition, operation, etc. of the Support Committee and the working committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 25 (Functions of the Support Committee)
The Support Committee shall deliberate on the following matters:
1. Matters concerning the support plan for areas hosting management facilities under Article 26;
2. Matters concerning the implementation plan for support for areas hosting management facilities under Article 27;
3. Other matters concerning support for areas hosting management facilities, etc. under this Act that the Chairperson of the Support Committee submits for consideration at a meeting.

Article 26 (Establishment of Support Plans for Areas Hosting Management Facilities)
(1) The Commission shall establish a support plan for areas hosting management facilities (hereinafter referred to as the "support plan") to provide support for areas hosting management facilities, etc. efficiently and systematically. In such cases, the Commission shall consult in advance with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies concerned with the support plan and the heads of the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas hosting management facilities, etc.
(2) The support plan shall be finalized following deliberation by the Support Committee.
(3) The support plan under paragraph (1) shall include the following matters: <Amended on June 2, 2026>
1. The objectives and basic direction of support for areas hosting management facilities, etc.;
2. Matters concerning the special support grant under Article 28;
3. Matters concerning the relocation of public institutions to local areas under Article 25 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth;
4. Matters concerning the management operator's support projects and preferential employment of local residents;
5. Matters concerning support for projects included in the comprehensive plan for the local era under Article 6 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth and the national land plans under Article 6 of the Framework Act on the National Land;
6. Required financial resources and a financing plan;
7. Other matters that the Support Committee deems necessary to support areas hosting management facilities, etc.
(4) The Commission may request cooperation from the heads of relevant central administrative agencies to provide effective support for areas hosting management facilities, etc. In such cases, the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
(5) Matters necessary regarding the procedures and requirements for establishing the support plan and the contents of that plan shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 27 (Formulation of Implementation Plans for Support for Areas Hosting Management Facilities)
(1) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall formulate and implement implementation plans for support for areas hosting management facilities for their respective areas of responsibility in order to implement the support plan.
(2) The heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall submit to the Commission the results of implementation of the implementation plans for support for areas hosting management facilities for the previous year and the implementation plans for the following year.
(3) Matters necessary for the procedures and requirements for formulating implementation plans for support for areas hosting management facilities and the contents of such plans shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 28 (Provision of Special Support Grants for Areas Hosting Management Facilities, etc.)
(1) The Commission may require the management operator to provide a special support grant for areas hosting management facilities, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "special support grant") to the local government having jurisdiction.
(2) Details such as the amount of the special support grant under paragraph (1) and the timing of its provision shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 29 (Establishment and Operation of a Special Account for Support Projects for Hosting Areas)
(1) A special account for support projects for hosting areas (hereinafter referred to as "special account") shall be established in the local government having jurisdiction in order to secure the funds required for support projects for areas hosting management facilities, etc. and to operate such funds in a rational manner.
(2) The special account shall be managed and operated by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the hosting area.
(3) The revenues of the special account shall be as follows:
1. The special support grant;
2. Fees accruing to the local government having jurisdiction pursuant to Article 40 (2);
3. Other proceeds from the management and operation of the special account, etc.
(4) The expenditures of the special account shall be as follows:
1. Expenses required for projects such as the establishment of medical facilities and health examinations;
2. Expenses required for projects such as the establishment of educational facilities and scholarship support;
3. Expenses required for projects such as regional development, tourism promotion, and the expansion of cultural facilities;
4. Expenses required for projects to increase the income of local residents, stabilize their livelihoods, improve their living environment, and promote their welfare, etc.;
5. Expenses required for other projects prescribed by Presidential Decree for the development of hosting areas and the improvement of residents' living conditions.

Article 30 (Construction of Underground Research Facilities, etc.)
(1) The Commission shall construct underground research facilities for research purposes and may undertake research necessary for the construction and operation of disposal facilities, international exchanges of related technologies and personnel, international joint research and development, etc.
(2) When a site for management facilities has been selected pursuant to Article 23 (2), the Commission shall, before designing and constructing a disposal facility, construct underground research facilities within the site of the disposal facility and research and demonstrate the performance of factors related to the safety of the disposal facility, incorporating the research findings under paragraph (1).
(3) Matters necessary for the construction and operation, etc. of underground research facilities under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 31 (Reconsideration of the Commission's Deliberation Results and Revocation of the Selection of Sites for Management Facilities)
(1) The Commission may reconsider deliberations and resolutions on the following matters if the Chairperson finds that important matters affecting the substance of deliberations have been omitted or that there is a material defect in the results of a site suitability survey:
1. Selection of sites for a preliminary survey under Article 21 (2);
2. Identification of sites for an in-depth survey under Article 22 (1);
3. Identification of proposed sites for management facilities under Article 23 (1).
(2) The Commission may revoke the selection of a site for management facilities selected pursuant to Article 23 (2) in any of the following cases:
1. Where an unforeseen serious problem concerning geological characteristics or safety arises during construction work on management facilities;
2. Where there is a material defect in the site suitability survey process, making it difficult to recognize the validity of residents' consent;
3. Where construction of management facilities becomes impossible due to a disaster or calamity.
(3) Revocation by the Commission of the selection of a site for management facilities pursuant to paragraph (2) shall be subject to the Commission's deliberation and resolution.
(4) When the Commission has revoked the selection of a site for management facilities pursuant to paragraph (2), it shall, without delay, notify the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the site and the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over an area within the extent prescribed by Presidential Decree of that fact and report it to the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.
(5) Where a site for management facilities is selected again after the selection of a site for management facilities has been revoked pursuant to paragraph (2), Articles 20 through 30 shall apply to the selection procedures and the site selected.

CHAPTER IV MANAGEMENT OF HIGH-LEVEL RADIOACTIVE WASTE, ETC.

Article 32 (Operating Standards for Management Facilities)
(1) The management operator shall establish standards for the operation of management facilities (hereinafter referred to as "operating standards") for the safe management of high-level radioactive waste.
(2) Where the management operator intends to establish, amend, or abolish operating standards, it shall obtain approval from the Commission: Provided, That where it intends to amend minor matters prescribed by rules of the Commission, it shall file a report with the Commission.
(3) The operating standards shall include the following matters:
1. Procedures and methods for the management of high-level radioactive waste at management facilities;
2. Inspection, maintenance, and repair of management facilities;
3. Other matters the Commission considers necessary for the safe operation of management facilities.

Article 33 (Development of Infrastructure for the Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste)
(1) The Commission shall develop infrastructure for the management of high-level radioactive waste, including technology development and human resources development, in order to manage high-level radioactive waste safely.
(2) In order to efficiently develop infrastructure for the management of high-level radioactive waste, the management operator shall formulate a plan for developing infrastructure for the management of high-level radioactive waste (hereinafter referred to as "infrastructure development plan") every five years, with a planning period of at least 10 years.
(3) When formulating an infrastructure development plan, the management operator shall submit it to the Commission and obtain its approval; the same shall apply to amendments to approved matters: Provided, That when amending minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, the management operator shall file a report with the Commission.
(4) Matters necessary for the formulation of infrastructure development plans under paragraph (2) and for approval and reporting under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 34 (Technology Development Projects for the Safe Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste)
(1) The Commission may undertake technology development projects, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, for the efficient and safe management of high-level radioactive waste.
(2) The Government may continuously pursue the development of technologies necessary for efficient management, including the reduction of volume and toxicity, in order to enhance the safety and economic efficiency of the management of spent nuclear fuel and high-level radioactive waste and reduce the burden of disposal, and may reflect the results of technology development in the master plan, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) To maintain coordination and consistency in the implementation of technology development projects for the safe management of high-level radioactive waste and to implement such projects efficiently, the Commission may have institutions or organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree undertake the planning, evaluation, and management of technology development projects for the safe management of high-level radioactive waste.

Article 35 (Projects for Training Specialized Personnel)
(1) The Commission may undertake projects to train personnel specializing in technologies for the management of high-level radioactive waste.
(2) To ensure a stable supply of specialized personnel necessary for the management of high-level radioactive waste, the Commission may designate the following institutions as institutions for training specialized personnel and have them undertake projects for training specialized personnel:
1. Universities, industrial universities, junior colleges, and technical colleges under the Higher Education Act, and polytechnic colleges under the National Lifelong Vocational Skills Development Act;
2. Specific research institutes under Article 2 of the Specific Research Institutes Promotion Act;
3. Government-funded science and technology research institutes under Article 2 of the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutes;
4. Other educational and training institutions in the field of radioactive waste prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(3) The Commission may revoke the designation of an institution for training specialized personnel designated pursuant to paragraph (2) if it falls under any of the following:
1. Where it obtained designation as an institution for training specialized personnel by false or improper means;
2. Where it no longer satisfies the requirements for designation as an institution for training specialized personnel.
(4) The Commission shall hold a hearing when revoking a designation pursuant to paragraph (3).
(5) Matters necessary for the scope of projects for training specialized personnel under paragraph (1), the designation of institutions for training specialized personnel under paragraph (2), the revocation of designations under paragraph (3), etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 36 (Installation and Operation of Spent Nuclear Fuel Storage Facilities Within Nuclear Power Plant Sites, etc.)
(1) Where an operator of a nuclear power reactor under Article 22 (1) of the Nuclear Safety Act intends to install spent nuclear fuel storage facilities within a nuclear power plant site (hereinafter referred to as "on-site storage facilities"), the operator shall, in consultation with the management operator, formulate a facility plan for the on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as "facility plan") before an amendment to the operating license is approved pursuant to the latter part of Article 20 (1) of the Nuclear Safety Act.
(2) When formulating a facility plan pursuant to paragraph (1), the person concerned shall solicit the opinions of residents pursuant to paragraph (4) and obtain approval from the Commission, as prescribed by Presidential Decree; the same shall apply where the person intends to amend approved matters: Provided, That when amending minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, the person shall file a report with the Chairperson.
(3) Where the Commission has approved a facility plan pursuant to paragraph (2), it shall include the facility plan in the master plan unless there are unavoidable reasons.
(4) A person who intends to formulate a facility plan pursuant to paragraph (1) shall solicit, through the following methods, the opinions of residents of areas surrounding on-site storage facilities within the extent prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as "areas surrounding on-site storage facilities"). In such cases, a public hearing, etc. shall be held if requested by the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the location of the relevant nuclear power plant or by residents of areas surrounding on-site storage facilities:
1. Online disclosure of information, and provision of information to the relevant local governments for public notice to residents and public inspection;
2. Information sessions and discussion meetings attended by domestic and foreign experts, etc.;
3. Other methods for soliciting opinions determined by the Commission.
(5) The methods and procedures for soliciting opinions under paragraph (4) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(6) The storage capacity of on-site storage facilities shall not exceed the quantity expected to be generated during the design life of the nuclear power reactors under construction or in operation at the relevant nuclear power plant.
(7) Spent nuclear fuel generated at other nuclear power plants shall not be brought into on-site storage facilities.
(8) Spent nuclear fuel stored in on-site storage facilities shall be transferred to management facilities without delay after construction of the management facilities is completed.
(9) A person who has formulated a facility plan pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2) shall cooperate with the activities of a body established and operated pursuant to the Act on Assistance to Electric Power Plants-Neighboring Areas and local government ordinances to monitor matters such as environmental and radiation safety in areas surrounding nuclear power plants, where that body seeks to monitor the environmental impact of on-site storage facilities and related safety activities.

Article 37 (Support for Areas Surrounding On-Site Storage Facilities)
(1) The Commission shall prepare support measures for areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as "support measures") in consultation with the person who has formulated a facility plan pursuant to Article 36 (1) and (2) and the head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas surrounding on-site storage facilities.
(2) The support measures shall include the following matters:
1. The total amount provided to support areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as "support funding");
2. The amount of support funding allocated to each zone prescribed by Presidential Decree within areas surrounding on-site storage facilities (hereinafter referred to as "support funding by zone");
3. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the amount of financial resources for each year.
(3) Support funding shall be determined in consideration of factors such as the storage capacity and operating period of on-site storage facilities, and support funding by zone shall be determined in consideration of factors such as the area and population of the relevant zone and its distance from the on-site storage facilities.
(4) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas surrounding on-site storage facilities shall formulate and implement a support project plan for areas surrounding on-site storage facilities financed by support funding by zone, after following the procedures prescribed by Presidential Decree, including soliciting the opinions of residents. In such cases, direct support projects for residents under paragraph (5) 1 shall be implemented within a limit of 50 percent of the total support funding allocated to the relevant zone.
(5) The types of support projects for areas surrounding on-site storage facilities shall be as follows:
1. Direct support projects for residents: Projects providing direct support to residents, such as payment of a specified amount;
2. Resident welfare projects: Projects supporting the installation of facilities to enhance convenience, improvement of the residential environment, etc.;
3. Income enhancement projects: Projects supporting enterprises and cooperatives jointly operated by residents, facilities for the storage and sale of products produced by residents, etc. in order to increase residents' income;
4. Educational support projects: Projects such as setting aside scholarship funds and providing dormitories;
5. Other projects necessary for the development of areas surrounding on-site storage facilities, environmental improvement, safety management, and the improvement of residents' health and quality of life.
(6) Details necessary for the implementation of paragraphs (1) through (5) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 38 (High-Level Radioactive Waste Management Operator)
(1) The management operator shall be the Korea Radioactive Waste Agency under Article 18 (1) of the Radioactive Waste Management Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Agency").
(2) The Agency shall be subject to the guidance and supervision of the Commission in respect of its functions related to the management of high-level radioactive waste, and the Commission may issue directions or orders to the Agency concerning its projects if it considers it necessary.

Article 39 (Use of Funds)
(1) The Radioactive Waste Management Fund under Article 28 of the Radioactive Waste Management Act may be used to provide the necessary support for projects prescribed by Presidential Decree for the management of high-level radioactive waste.
(2) The Nuclear Energy Research and Development Account of the Nuclear Energy Fund under Article 17 of the Nuclear Energy Promotion Act may be used to provide the necessary support for projects prescribed by Presidential Decree for research and development associated with the management of high-level radioactive waste.

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 40 (Collection and Allocation of Fees)
(1) The management operator may collect fees from persons delivering high-level radioactive waste, based on the quantity of high-level radioactive waste received pursuant to Article 13(1) of the Radioactive Waste Management Act, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Of the fees collected under paragraph (1), an amount corresponding to the percentage prescribed by Presidential Decree shall accrue to the competent local government, and the remainder shall accrue to the management operator.
(3) Matters necessary for the allocation procedures under paragraph (2) and other related matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 41 (Reports and Inspections, etc.)
(1) Where the Commission deems it necessary for the safe and efficient management of high-level radioactive waste, it may require generators of high-level radioactive waste and management operators to make reports or submit materials, as prescribed by the Commission, and may have relevant public officials enter offices, places of business, etc. to inspect relevant documents, facilities, equipment, etc.
(2) When conducting an inspection under paragraph (1), the person subject to inspection shall be notified of the inspection plan, including the date and time, reasons, and details of the inspection, no later than seven days before the inspection. However, this shall not apply where the inspection is deemed urgent or where it is deemed that the purpose of the inspection cannot be achieved due to the destruction of evidence or other such circumstances.
(3) A public official conducting entry and inspection under paragraph (1) shall carry a certificate indicating their authority and present it to the persons concerned.
(4) Where necessary for matters such as the formulation of a support plan, the Commission may, as prescribed by the Commission, require the head of a Si/Gun/Gu with jurisdiction over areas hosting management facilities, etc. to report details of the use of the special support grant and the fees under Article 40, or order the submission of materials.
(5) Where an investigation to verify the facts is necessary as a result of reviewing the contents of the reports and materials under paragraph (4), the Commission may have relevant public officials conduct such an investigation.
(6) When conducting an investigation under paragraph (5), the competent local government shall be notified in advance of the date and time, reasons, and details of the investigation, etc., and a public official conducting the investigation shall carry a certificate indicating their authority and present it to the persons concerned.

Article 42 (Orders to Take Measures Issued to Generators of High-Level Radioactive Waste, etc.)
(1) Where the Commission deems that the failure of generators of high-level radioactive waste and management operators to fulfill their obligations under this Act poses a risk of significantly impeding the management of high-level radioactive waste, it may set an appropriate period and order rectification or necessary measures, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) Before issuing an order under paragraph (1), the Commission shall notify the generators of high-level radioactive waste and management operators of the reasons for the order and give them an opportunity to submit opinions and evidence. However, where immediate action is required for the safe management of high-level radioactive waste, it shall give them an opportunity to submit opinions and evidence afterward.

Article 43 (Vicarious Execution)
Where generators of high-level radioactive waste and management operators that have received an order under Article 42 fail to comply with that order, the Commission may carry out vicarious execution as prescribed by the Administrative Vicarious Execution Act.

Article 44 (Entrustment of Duties)
The Commission may entrust the following of its powers under this Act to the management operator, as prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. The preliminary site suitability survey under Article 21;
2. The in-depth site suitability survey under Article 22;
3. Other duties prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 45 (Deeming Persons Public Officials for the Application of Penalty Provisions)
Any of the following persons who is not a public official shall be deemed a public official for the purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act:
1. Members of the Commission and staff of the Secretariat;
2. Executive officers and employees of a management operator engaged in duties entrusted by the Commission pursuant to Article 44.

CHAPTER VI PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 46 (Penalty Provisions)
(1) A person who destroys or improperly operates management facilities, thereby endangering a person's life or physical safety or harming public safety, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one year and not more than ten years.
(2) A person who kills a person or causes a person's death by committing an offense under paragraph (1) shall be punished by death, imprisonment for life, or imprisonment for not less than seven years.
(3) Attempts to commit an offense under paragraph (1) or (2) shall be punishable.
(4) A person who engages in preparation, conspiracy, or incitement for the purpose of committing an offense under paragraph (1) or (2) shall be punished by imprisonment for a fixed term of not less than one year.

Article 47 (Penalty Provisions)
(1) A person who obstructs the management of high-level radioactive waste by damaging or stealing management facilities or disrupting their functions shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than ten years or by a fine not exceeding 100 million won.
(2) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than five years or by a fine not exceeding 50 million won:
1. A person who obstructs the management of high-level radioactive waste by operating management facilities without justifiable grounds;
2. A person working at management facilities who, without justifiable grounds, fails to maintain or operate the management facilities, thereby disrupting the management of high-level radioactive waste.
(3) Attempts to commit an offense under paragraph (1) or subparagraph 1 of paragraph (2) shall be punishable.

Article 48 (Penalty Provisions)
(1) A person other than a management operator who undertakes the management of high-level radioactive waste, the selection of sites for management facilities, or the construction, operation, or post-closure management of management facilities shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won, or by both.
(2) A person who carries out an implementation plan without obtaining approval, in violation of the main clause of Article 19(2), shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or by a fine not exceeding 20 million won, or by both.
(3) A person who carries out an implementation plan without obtaining approval for changes, in violation of the main clause of Article 19(2), shall be punished by a fine not exceeding 3 million won.

Article 49 (Joint Penalty Provisions)
(1) If a representative, agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation commits a violation under Article 47 or 48 in connection with the business of the corporation, the corporation shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to the punishment imposed on the offender. However, this shall not apply if the corporation has not neglected to exercise due care and supervision over the relevant business to prevent such violation.
(2) If an agent, employee, or other worker of an individual commits a violation under Article 47 or 48 in connection with the business of that individual, the individual shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to the punishment imposed on the offender. However, this shall not apply if the individual has not neglected to exercise due care and supervision over the relevant business to prevent such violation.

Article 50 (Administrative Fines)
(1) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 2 million won:
1. A person who fails to report a change, in violation of the proviso to Article 19(2);
2. A person who fails to make a report or submit materials under Article 41(1) or (4), or makes a false report or submits false materials;
3. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades entry or inspection under Article 41(1) or an investigation under Article 41(5);
4. A person who fails to comply with an order under Article 42(1).
(2) The administrative fines under paragraph (1) shall be imposed and collected by the Commission, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 20843, March 25, 2025>

Article 1 (Entry into Force)
This Act shall enter into force on the date on which six months have elapsed after its promulgation.

Article 2 (Preparatory Acts for the Enforcement of This Act)
Preparations for the establishment of the Commission, including the appointment or commissioning of members and staff of the Commission and the enactment and promulgation of the Commission's rules concerning the enforcement of this Act, may be undertaken before this Act enters into force.

Article 3 (Application to the Commencement of Terms of Office of Commission Members)
The term of office of a member first appointed or commissioned under this Act shall be deemed to commence on the date of the member's appointment or commissioning.

Article 4 (Application to On-Site Storage Facilities)
Article 36(6) through (8) shall also apply to on-site storage facilities whose construction was completed or commenced before this Act enters into force.

Article 5 (Transitional Measure Concerning Article 36-2 of the Nuclear Safety Act)
Through October 22, 2025, the reference to "Article 36-2 of the Nuclear Safety Act" in the proviso to subparagraph 2 of Article 2 shall be deemed a reference to "Article 35(4) of the Nuclear Safety Act".

Article 6 (Transitional Measures Concerning Affairs under Jurisdiction, etc.)
(1) Of the affairs previously under the jurisdiction of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment at the time this Act enters into force, the affairs under Article 7(1) shall be taken over by the Commission under this Act. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(2) Among the public notices, administrative dispositions, and other acts performed by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, and the applications, reports, and other acts made to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment before this Act enters into force, those concerning matters whose jurisdiction is transferred from the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment to the Commission shall be deemed acts of the Commission or acts made to the Commission. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 7 (Amendment of Another Act)
The Electric Power Source Development Promotion Act is partially amended as follows.

In Article 3, "power generation business operators, power transmission business operators, and radioactive waste management operators under Article 10 of the Radioactive Waste Management Act" shall be replaced with "power generation business operators, power transmission business operators, radioactive waste management operators under Article 10 of the Radioactive Waste Management Act, and high-level radioactive waste management operators under Article 38 of the Special Act on the Management of High-Level Radioactive Waste".

Article 8 (Relationship with Other Statutes and Regulations)
With respect to the affairs under Article 7(1) taken over by the Commission pursuant to this Act, where other statutes or regulations refer to the "Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment" or the "Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment" at the time this Act enters into force, such references shall be deemed references to the "High-Level Radioactive Waste Management Commission" or the "Chairperson of the High-Level Radioactive Waste Management Commission", respectively, in accordance with the matters prescribed in those statutes or regulations. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
